text:
Tuttosport reports that Alexander Sorloth remains Luciano Spalletti’s favourite attacking target, but Juventus would only welcome the Atletico Madrid forward on loan with an option to buy.
Juventus are expected to be busy in the January transfer window, as the Serie A giants will look for a new central midfielder, a left-back, and a centre-forward.
It is no secret that the Bianconeri will have limited financial resources for the winter transfer window, forcing the club to focus on targets potentially available at a low price.
This is not believed to be the case for Folarin Balogun, who is no longer part of Monaco’s plans but was close to joining Everton for €50m last summer, a fee the Old Lady can’t afford.
Gianluca Scamacca of Atalanta is also being monitored by the Bianconeri, but according to Tuttosport, Atletico Madrid’s Alexander Sorloth remains Spalletti’s top target.
Juventus already held talks with Atletico and Sorloth last summer, when Spalletti even spoke directly with the Norwegian international.
Ironically, Sorloth is getting less game time than last season because of Juventus loanee Jonathan David, so he is considering leaving the Wanda Metropolitano in January.
According to Tuttosport, Spalletti favours Sorloth for his eye for goal and physicality. Spalletti wants a classic centre-forward, as Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade aren’t entirely suited to his style.
Tuttosport, however, warns that Juventus would only consider signing Sorloth on loan with an option to buy, as they are unwilling to commit to a future permanent transfer for a player who will turn 31 in December.
